non_blocking.what: Carried from pass 1. A regex cannot be interrupted, so the climb only protects against patterns that become slow within a few 15 % steps. A contrived pattern within the 300-character cap (about 40 repeated '(a*)' groups followed by 'b') measured 13.4 s inside validateWhen before it was rejected. Disclosed by the coder and accepted; a caller on the host main thread (rules_propose, loop_propose) should know validateWhen can take seconds on a hostile pattern.

Carried from pass 1. The regex is compiled on every matchesFilter call and a pattern that bypassed validateWhen (hand-edited file) runs against up to 8 KiB without a probe. Callers that load files (FEAT-003, FEAT-010) must call validateWhen on read; a compile cache is worth adding when the rules gate (FEAT-006) calls it before every tool call.

Carried from pass 1. The rules design allows a detector 'every' of at least 60 s while validateWhen with action 'work' refuses under 300 s. Detectors are a blocked step (R6); R6 has to validate the detector floor itself or get a distinct action value.

A computed value is raised to the entry minimum (gate 1 s, work 5 s) and rounded up, so an estimate of 2 s on a work script returns 5 s, not 2 s. Disclosed as interpretation 3 in the FEAT findings and needed so the result always passes validateScriptAction; recorded here so the later recorder of timeout changes does not read 'estimate' as 'the estimate verbatim'.
